text: [Coit Drapery Cleaners, Inc. v. Sequoia Ins. Co., supra, 14 CA4th at 1613, 18 CR2d at 704-705] • [3:452] Corporation's President sexually harassed female employees. He had founded the corporation, and was a major stockholder, chairman of its board of directors, and the corporation's “managing agent.” Because his acts were known to and ratified and condoned by the corporation, it could not claim insurance coverage for the liability created by President's acts: “[I]t would be contrary to public policy to allow a wrongdoer which is directly and strictly liable for such wrongdoing, such as Coit, to shift the loss resulting from such an unlawful corporate practice to its insurer.” [Coit Drapery Cleaners, Inc. v. Sequoia Ins. Co., supra, 14 CA4th at 1606-1607, 18 CR2d at 700] (b) [3:453] Compare—respondeat superior liability: However, § 533 does not bar indemnification for sexual harassment claims based entirely on vicarious liability (respondeat superior) and for which the corporation is not otherwise at fault.
